cut_when.why: one Content ID claim blocks a Short over 60s worldwide

youtube_shorts._cut_note: Audit call 5 (2026-10-17, decided as recommended): a YouTube Short over 60s with any copyright claim is blocked worldwide; at 60s or less it stays up and the claimant takes the money. So a network or C-SPAN clip (rights rebroadcast: a network, C-SPAN, podcast or creator copy) over 60s goes to YouTube only as its own 30-59s cut (youtube.mp4 beside the clip: factory.py ytcut in the nightly run, like Instagram's). With no cut it does not post to YouTube and its card says why. Owned clips (committee, member, White House feeds) go whole, and so does a clip with no rights on record (a hand drop has no job, so ytcut cannot cut it: "unknown" in cut_when.rights would keep every long drop off YouTube).

_volume_how: Per account (2026-10-20, Lab): "volume" is a list of dated rules, each {"from": YYYY-MM-DD or left out, "until": YYYY-MM-DD or left out, "slots": [the day's slots, a subset of "slots"], "why": a few words}. A NEW board for a day takes the first rule whose dates hold that day (no rule: the first daily_target slots, as every other account). No two rules may cover one day, and a bad rule stops the config with one line. A board keeps the slots it was made with: factory.py plan <account> --date D says when the rule differs, and --resync adds the missing slots as open and takes out open slots the rule no longer lists. daily_target stays the most a day ever has (the YouTube 24-hour cap reads it).
_outlets_how: Per platform: "export" (SCHEDULE.csv + Ready to post folders) or "api" (posts by itself: YouTube at schedule time with publishAt, the others from `factory.py post-due` at the slot). Sign in first: factory.py connect youtube|meta|tiktok <account>. TikTok goes through Andrew's own app, AJJ Clip Factory (sent for TikTok's review 2026-10-17): "export" (by hand) until TikTok approves it, then "api" with "api_app_audited": true. Upload-Post ("via": "upload-post") is unused code. "from": an ISO time before which that outlet's slots stay by hand.
_posting_switches_how: Owner switches (2026-10-17 audit; ON since that night, off when absent): signed_by_hand_stays (per account: a slot signed while a platform was by hand stays by hand after that platform switches to api), upload_ahead_hours + upload_gap_minutes (per youtube_shorts outlet: upload a slot only that close to its time, never two uploads closer than the gap), tags_from_hashtags (per youtube_shorts outlet: the description's hashtags become the video's tags), inbox_auto_sign (top level: false = a dropped clip waits for Approve)
_links_how: Per account: short = its name on the Clip Review calendar and in the morning notice; links = its public profile on each platform, opened from the account's header in Clip Review.
_active_how: Per account (2026-10-19): "active": false keeps the block while nothing is made, scheduled or posted for it (doctor lists what it still needs); no key = on. "machine": the computer that runs it (CLIP_FACTORY_MACHINE on that computer; no key = "main", this Mac). "kit": its brand kit in the skill (assets/brand/<kit>, presets/<kit>.json; Gaming's is gta). "job_tag": a word in its skill jobs' names (factory-<tag>-<date>-...). "scout_minute": the minute its hourly scout runs once it is switched on (a GTA account other than Gaming; without it, 6 minutes per place after Gaming's :40).
_social_how: The social layer (Clip Review's Inbox, Cards, Reports and Log tabs; clipfactory/social.py) ships off for every account. Its switches are per account in state/<account>/social/settings.json: Clip Review, Log, Switches, or factory.py social on|off <account> <part>. Nothing in this file switches them. Stop everything on the Log tab halts every comment, reply, message, story and card; signed clips keep posting.
_inbox_auto_sign_note: false since 2026-10-17 20:30 (Andrew: implement every audit call; call 2 'land drops as Ready'): a clip dropped in the drop folder waits in its slot as a ready clip until Andrew presses Approve (with the automatic sign-off on, it signs itself 30 minutes before its slot like every ready clip).
_auto_sign_how: The automatic sign-off (clipfactory/autosign.py), ON since 2026-10-19 (Andrew: 'Yes. Build the automatic sign-off: every clip that passed its checks signs itself 30 minutes before its slot, signed as the factory, not me. Clips naming 2 or more people nobody checked still wait for me.'). post-due (every 10 minutes) signs each ready clip lead_minutes before its slot as 'Clip Factory (auto)', the same signature and checks as Approve, never Andrew's name, never a cast.json verified. It skips a clip a person pulled (until a person approves it), a slot more than late_hours past, a Not them hold, a stand-in, and per cast_unchecked: one = a clip naming 2 or more people no person checked waits (one person named in the source title signs), all = those sign too, none = any unchecked cast waits. An account's own auto_sign block changes any key for it; a client account signs itself only by its own block. on false = Approve only (the old way). coach_gate (since 2026-10-30, the loops thesis item 1): shadow = the hook coach's one word on each clip that signs itself (PASS, FIX or KILL) is written to state/<slug>/coach/gate-shadow.jsonl and holds nothing; off = not looked at. Holding a FIX or KILL waits until the shadow nights are read.
